separation: AIO CLIENT IDENTITY ≠ LOGIN EMAIL ≠ OPTIONAL AIO ALIAS

business_identity.rule: Issued once per business from the existing sequence aio_next_customer_number() (AIO-CUS- + 6 digits), stored on the organisation, never reused, never derived from an email. Plain AIO-###### is already the service-request number format (aio_next_request_number), so a client ID must not use it.
business_identity.issued_at: APPROVE MIGRATION (existing client) · intake completion or CRM conversion (new client)
business_identity.founder_question: Display format: AIO-CUS-001042 (existing primitive) or a shorter AIO-C-1042 — not AIO-1042 (collides with request numbers).

login_email.rule: The deliverable email the client signs in with (Supabase auth user). Replaceable only through a verified credential-change flow (verify the new address before switching). Never the business identity.

alias.rule: Optional AIO-branded alias (for example an AIO mailbox name) kept as a separate attribute. Never required to authenticate; AIO does not need to run a mailbox system for clients to sign in.

flow: YOUR AIO OFFICE IS READY (email: company name · AIO client ID · secure link)
server verifies the token hash + expiry
client sets their own password (updateUser) — or signs in by magic link
server links the auth user to the organisation (membership, status active)

existing.note: not used; detectSessionInUrl is on, so link sessions would be picked up
no server function holds the service-role key yet

existing.capability: link an existing organisation to a new user
existing.note: membership user_id is NOT NULL — the membership is created at acceptance, not at invitation

proposed.invitation_store: aio_client_activation_invites (organization_id, email, token_sha256, issued_at, expires_at, state, sent_by, accepted_user_id) — single use; plain token never stored
proposed.route: /office-activation/:token (token-route precedent /quote/:secureToken; “/activate” already names the start-your-business compliance step)
proposed.server: activation endpoint with the service-role key: verify token → create or find the auth user → membership (organization_owner, active) → lifecycle CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED
proposed.magic_link: optional sign-in method after activation (signInWithOtp); the invitation token still decides which organisation is linked

must_fix_before_activation.what: RLS lets any signed-in user insert a membership into any organisation

Self sign-up always creates a new organisation — a migrated client who signs up would duplicate their business (route known emails to “check your invitation / contact AIO”, never auto-link without the token)
Password-reset link points at a route that does not exist
The portal never reads account status — a pending client would get the full portal

template.subject: Your AIO office is ready
body: This link works once and expires {expires_at}. AIO will never send you a password.
template.channel: email via the communication engine (templates model communicationTypes.ts:212; provider not configured — demo adapters only)

passwords.rule: The client sets their own password on the activation page (or signs in by magic link). AIO never generates, stores in plain text, emails, texts or reads out a password.

findings_in_aio.today: No temporary or generated password exists anywhere in AIO; every password is typed by the user and goes straight to Supabase Auth. Nothing emails or texts a password.
findings_in_aio.risk: With no invite / magic-link primitive, an activation flow could be tempted to mint and send passwords. Forbidden by this contract.

at_activation: ELECTRONIC_COMMUNICATIONS (email; SMS only if opted in)
consents.store: aio_consents (user_id, consent_type, version, granted_at, revoked_at — all-in-one-enterprises/supabase/migrations/20260815140000_aio_integrations_security_audit.sql:72; unused today) + CommConsentRecord for channels (all-in-one-enterprises/src/communications/communicationTypes.ts:189)
consents.today: Terms acceptance is validated on sign-up but never persisted in backend mode.
consents.not_at_activation: Service authorisations (POA · BOC-3 · IFTA authorisation) belong to the workspace that needs them, not to activation.
consents.founder_question: Confirm the legally required set and wording.
